_comment: A round takes roundMinutes of real time, whatever the world speed, so reinforcements can come. A unit's attack and defense are ranges: each round every unit type strikes with its attack × a roll within 1 ± statSpread, and every target type takes it on its defense × such a roll (a card shows 10–16 for 13 ± 25%). Damage = count × rolled attack × stance attack × matchup × counter × target share × casualtyScale; the target's rolled defense is armor, letting armorConstant / (armorConstant + defense) of it through (as armor does in an RPG); what lands, over the target's health (units.json, enemies.json) × stance defense × home bonus, is how many fall. A side breaks once it has lost retreatAt of its starting units (null: never): risk against reward, the earlier a stance breaks the more it gives. On the players' side every army fights in its own stance and breaks on its own losses (since it joined the battle), falling back home beaten (its hero wounded, its general killed) while the others fight on; a village's garrison fights in the village's stance, and a garrison that breaks stops fighting. The defenders lose once every army and the garrison has broken or fallen. Afflictions: a unit that burns (its own inflicts, or forged fire arrows) hurts its targets again with `burn.share` of its blow in each of the next `burn.rounds` rounds, through armor as any blow; a side struck by a unit that poisons fights at `poison.factor` of its attack and defense for the next `poison.rounds` rounds.

terrain._comment: Where a battle is fought changes how hard each side hits and holds. Each feature of the battle's hex (terrain.json ground: flat, woods, hills, wetland), and each mountain beside it and each river along it or lake beside it (mountain, water; at most maxStack of each count), adds its share to a unit's attack or defense: its family's below, its own (units.json terrain) and, for the players, their clan's (clans.json effects terrain.<feature>.<attack|defense>). They add up; the sum multiplies the stat.

lines._comment: Armies meet in a battle line, and the smaller army sets its width: the larger one fights with as many of its troops as the smaller has, the rest wait behind (they strike only when a maneuver brings them in). Round 1 is an exchange of missiles: only archers shoot, at the enemy's infantry. From round 2 the larger side may maneuver, up to its commander's cap (none, flank, pincer, encircle). flank: on flat land (with or without woods) cavalry of flank.ratio times the enemy's, on hills infantry; the surplus strikes at surplusDealt and takes surplusTaken of the blows. pincer: on flat land cavalry pincer.ratio times the enemy's or cavalry and infantry together pincer.mixedRatio times, on hills infantry (or infantry and cavalry); it needs a commander (a general of commander.general, a hero with Battle Fury commander.battleFury, on flat land Horse Lord commander.horseLord, on hills Spearhead commander.spearhead, a horde's leader of commander.leader), and no mountain, river or lake beside the battle. encircle: all troops encircle.ratio times the enemy's; every unit strikes at dealt and takes taken; never around a fort by the water. A maneuver whose surplus the smaller side destroys (its ratio no longer met against the smaller side as it was when the maneuver began) turns into a breakthrough: the smaller side strikes at the maneuver's dealt + breakthrough.dealtBonus and takes its taken, diluted by any troops that joined it since; the larger loses its maneuver for the rest of the battle. A side led by a Shield Bearer of shieldBearer.rank keeps its flank through a breakthrough and, outmaneuvered, takes shieldBearer.taken of the blows. A player's road through the battle's hex lowers the ratios by road.ratioCut and the commander's ranks by road.rankCut. A fort's holders need fort.holderFactor of every ratio, the side attacking them fort.attackerFactor. At a bridge the front is half the smaller side's infantry wide: no more troops of each side than that fight, nor archers, and nobody maneuvers.
